chains.title: Alt G disrupts a GATA half-site/composite motif in the BCL11A erythroid enhancer (DHS +62), reducing GATA1 binding, lowering BCL11A and raising HbF
chains.element: BCL11A intron-2 erythroid enhancer, cCRE EH38E2001346 (chr2:60490828-60491157)

links.claim: Fine-mapping of this BCL11A enhancer identified a motif-disrupting common variant with reduced TF binding, modestly lower BCL11A and higher HbF; ENCODE K562 GATA1 ChIP shows 2 peaks within 100 bp of the variant although none contains the exact base, consistent with a GATA-occupied region whose motif is weakened by the G allele. GATA1 was not among the QBiC-SELEX groups reported here, so no in vitro allelic score is cited for it
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 5.1, H3K27ac z 3.4; biosample maxima) that the literature describes as the essential erythroid enhancer of BCL11A containing the GWAS SNPs

The element is intronic to BCL11A, 63.6 kb from its TSS; credible sets containing this variant have PIP 1.00 with best L2G for BCL11A 0.89, and genome engineering showed the enhancer is required for BCL11A expression
The enhancer is required in erythroid but not B-lymphoid cells, and the variant's associations are erythroid (MCH, RBC count, reticulocyte volume, HbF/F-cells)
BCL11A is the repressor of gamma-globin; modestly reduced enhancer output lowers BCL11A and raises HbF, consistent with G being the HbF-raising effect allele and with milder sickle cell disease

predictions: Allele-specific GATA1 (and TAL1) ChIP in heterozygous erythroid cells shows T-biased occupancy at chr2:60490908
Single-base editing of T>G in HUDEP-2/CD34+ erythroid cells modestly lowers BCL11A and raises HBG1/2 without a myeloid or B-cell effect
Allelic MPRA of this enhancer fragment gives lower activity for G in erythroid but not lymphoid cells
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA1/TAL1 ChIP shows no imbalance at this base
Isolated base editing of rs1427407 leaves BCL11A and HBG unchanged while a linked +58 edit does
No GATA motif sequence is present at or adjacent to the variant

No allele-specific TF footprint or ChIP imbalance at chr2:60490908 in erythroid cells
Haplotypes carrying G but not the linked causal allele show normal HbF

grades_v0.reason: Only a QBiC-SELEX prediction. ELF1 is a passing member of G003 (z -11.29) and its 32.2 TPM is real, but the group's best model is ETV3, and the ELF1 effect size and site strength are not given. The choice of ELF1 rests on expression, not on a variant-specific ELF1 result. G020 does not support ELF1 as a passing member. No ChIP or allelic data.

E03 places the variant in a dELS cCRE (DNase z 5.1, H3K27ac z 3.4), but these are maxima across biosamples and not specific to erythroid cells. VEP lists no regulatory feature. Overlap with the +62 enhancer is asserted, not shown.

The variant is intronic to BCL11A. Credible sets at this variant have PIP 1.00 and L2G for BCL11A of 0.64-0.89, and the HbF in SCA set has L2G 0.70. This is genetic support for BCL11A as the gene, though not proof that this variant acts through ELF1.

Erythroid red-cell indices and HbF associations in E04/E05 fit an erythroid setting. K-562 expression of ELF1 is a proxy only, and E08 does not show erythroid activity of the enhancer. No erythroid-specific epigenomic data.

G is the effect allele for HbF in one set (PMID 34283174), and PMID 32563256 links the SNP to HbF >10%. This supports the locus-to-HbF link but not the ETS loss mechanism. The direction chain (G loses ETS, BCL11A down, HbF up) is untested, with no perturbation.

Own-model QBiC-SELEX z 42.63 with alt gain is a prediction only, from a single model (a 7-mer model of a C2H2 ZF). No ChIP or allelic data. A KRAB-ZF TF predicted from a single 7-mer is low confidence.
The same cCRE context as H1 applies (maxima over biosamples, not erythroid-specific).
The BCL11A intron location and credible-set L2G scores support BCL11A, as for H1.
ZNF493 at 17.9 TPM in K-562 shows only that it is expressed in the proxy. There is no evidence of a repressive KRAB-ZF role in erythroid precursors.
The claimed mechanism (gained repressor lowers BCL11A, raising HbF) has no direct evidence. E04/E06a only show G associated with higher HbF. Nothing links ZNF493 or KRAB repression to BCL11A or HbF.

The claim is inconsistent with E08 and E17. SPI1 is listed as a covered TF in G020, but it is not a passing member (passing members are ETV7, ELF3, ETV6, ELF5). In G049 the members disagree in direction, and SPIB, the best model, shows alt gain (z +21). SPI1 z -14.11 is a lone dissenting model. The claim that SPI1 loses binding with G is thinly supported and conflicts with its group's best model.
Same cCRE context, with no specific erythroid or myeloid data.
The BCL11A intron location and credible-set L2G scores support BCL11A, as for H1.
The cited E17 shows only the TPM of SPI1 in K-562. PU.1 is a myeloid/progenitor factor, and nothing links it to the erythroid role needed for HbF.
The HbF association supports the locus only. Nothing supports PU.1-driven BCL11A regulation.

RELA own-model z -31.14 is a prediction only. The claim of the largest effect size is wrong, since NFKB2 has effect -1.964 and TEAD1 -1.908, versus RELA -1.256. The percentile change is small (99.8 to 98.8), meaning the site stays strong, so abolition is overstated.
Same cCRE context, with high DNase but not erythroid-specific.
Credible-set L2G for BCL11A and the intronic location support BCL11A over REL and PAPOLG, which are over 265 kb away.
RELA expression in K-562 only. NF-kB activity in erythroid precursors is not shown.
The HbF association supports the locus only. No NF-kB link to BCL11A or HbF is provided.

grades_final.reason: E20b supports a motif-disrupting variant with reduced TF binding, but the quote names no TF and no GATA motif at this base. E19 shows no GATA1 peak contains the base. E20 is only a list of hits. GATA1 is not in QBiC coverage, so there is no allelic score. This is indirect and does not name GATA1.
E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E2001346 with DNase z 5.1 and H3K27ac z 3.4. E20a and E20d describe the GWAS SNPs as lying in an essential erythroid BCL11A enhancer.
E20d and E20c report genome engineering showing the enhancer is required for BCL11A expression. E05 gives L2G of 0.89 for BCL11A with PIP 1.00, and E02 shows the variant is intronic.
E20c shows the enhancer is required in erythroid but not B-lymphoid cells. E05 and E04 give erythroid trait associations (MCH, RBC count, HbF).

E20e links BCL11A to HbF regulation and E04 and E06a link the variant to HbF. E04 gives G as the effect allele for HbF in only one entry, and no cited evidence shows the G allele lowers BCL11A. E20b says only 'modestly diminished BCL11A expression'. The sickle severity link is by association only.

E16 shows ETS models losing binding on G, which is direction-consistent with ref binding more. ELF1 is chosen from the group on expression with no variant-specific effect. E18 shows no ELF1 ChIP peak at the variant. This is a binding prediction only.
E03 gives a dELS cCRE with strong accessibility, but only as biosample maxima that are not erythroid-specific. E01 adds nothing about ETS.
E05 gives credible sets with PIP 1.00 and L2G of 0.89 for BCL11A, and E02 shows the variant is intronic to BCL11A. This is genetic evidence for the gene link.
E04 and E05 show erythroid traits. E16 gives ETS TPM in K562 as context only. No evidence ties ETS factors to the enhancer in erythroid cells.
E04 and E06a link the variant to HbF, and E20e links BCL11A to HbF. The chain from ETS loss to lower BCL11A is not shown by any cited evidence.
E09 gives a single own-model prediction (z 42.63) that the alt allele binds ZNF493 more. There is no ChIP or allelic data.
E03 shows a dELS cCRE with maxima across biosamples. This gives only generic enhancer context and no link to ZNF493.
E02 shows the variant is intronic to BCL11A and E05 gives L2G of 0.89 for BCL11A with PIP 1.00.
E09 shows ZNF493 is expressed at 17.9 TPM in K562, but the chain itself notes no erythroid role is documented. This is expression context only.
E04 and E06a link the variant to HbF, but nothing links ZNF493 to BCL11A repression. The repressor mechanism is speculative and not shown by any evidence.
E10 shows an own RELA model losing binding on G, but the percentile drop is small (99.8 to 98.8). E11 gives NFKB2 as a stronger model effect. RELA is picked on expression. This is a prediction only.
E03 shows a dELS cCRE with high DNase, as biosample maxima. This is generic context with no link to NF-kB.
E02 shows the variant is intronic to BCL11A and E05 gives L2G of 0.89 for BCL11A against the distant REL/PAPOLG.
E10 shows RELA expression in K562 only. The chain admits NF-kB activity in erythroid precursors is not shown.
E04 and E06a link the variant to HbF, and E20e links BCL11A to HbF. No evidence connects NF-kB to BCL11A output or to this variant.
